lesson.title: Orthogonal and unit vectors

steps.headline: Orthogonal vectors have a dot product of zero. A unit vector has length 1.

lead.text: Two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero: they meet at a right angle. A unit vector has length 1. A set of vectors that are orthogonal and all unit is orthonormal.
Vector (1, 2) goes 1 across and 2 up. Vector (−2, 1) goes 2 back and 1 up. Find their dot product.

reveal.text: You found that the two products cancel. A dot product of zero means the vectors are orthogonal: the arrows meet at a right angle.

workedSteps.text: Divide every coordinate by the length.

steps.headline: Find the x coordinate of the unit vector in the direction (3, 4).

workedSteps.text: Divide the x coordinate by the length. Give it as a decimal.

lead.text: The length of a vector is never negative. Dividing by it keeps the signs of the coordinates.

reveal.text: You divided by a positive length, so the sign of the coordinate was kept. The result is a unit vector that still points the same way.

lead.text: A game turns a velocity into a direction by dividing it by its length. A character is standing still, so its velocity is (0, 0).

lesson.orientation: Recognise perpendicular vectors and turn a nonzero vector into a unit vector.
lesson.nextAction: Try the next idea, then return for a fresh problem after a delay.

blocks.text: A step of (6, 8) metres is 10 m long. You want a step in exactly the same direction that is only 1 m long.

intro.promise: By the end you'll test whether two vectors are perpendicular, and shrink any nonzero vector to length 1.

recap.keyIdea: Vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is zero. Dividing a nonzero vector by its length gives a unit vector in the same direction.

blocks.text: You found (1, 2) · (−2, 1) = 0, turned (3, 4) into a unit vector with x = 0.6, and saw that (0, 0) cannot be normalised because its length is zero.

recap.nextHook: Matrices store whole tables of numbers. First you need to read their rows and columns.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The step is 10 m long and should be 1 m, so multiply by 1/10 = 0.1.

questions.prompt: By what number do you multiply (6, 8) to get that 1 m step?
hints: How long is the step now?
You must shrink the length down to the wanted one. What fraction of the length is that?
Divide the wanted length by the current length.

misconceptions.feedback: That multiplies by the length, which makes the step ten times longer.

questions.onCorrect: 0.1. Scaling by one over the length gives length 1 and keeps the direction.

questions.prompt: Which pair of vectors is orthogonal?
hints: Find each pair's dot product. Which one gives zero?

misconceptions.feedback: Their dot product is not zero: the products 2 and 6 add up.
Their dot product is not zero: both products are positive, so they cannot cancel.

questions.onCorrect: Orthogonal means a dot product of zero: 1 − 1 = 0.

hints: Multiply matching coordinates.
One product is negative.
Add the two products. Do they cancel?

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The products −2 and 2 cancel, so the vectors are orthogonal.

misconceptions.feedback: Check the sign of the first product: one of its entries is negative.

questions.onCorrect: The products cancel, so the dot product is zero. Zero means orthogonal.

acceptedIdeas: Dividing by the length shrinks the vector to length 1 without turning it.
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Dividing every coordinate by the same positive number shrinks the arrow and keeps its direction.

questions.prompt: Why do we divide by the length to make a unit vector?

choices.label: Dividing by the length shrinks the vector to length 1 without turning it.
Dividing by the length makes the vector orthogonal.
Dividing by the length removes its minus signs.

hints: Think what dividing by a number does to every coordinate.

misconceptions.feedback: Orthogonal is about two vectors meeting at a right angle. Scaling one vector never turns it.
Signs stay: the length is positive, so each coordinate keeps its sign.

questions.onCorrect: A positive scalar shrinks the arrow without turning it. Dividing by the length makes it exactly 1.

questions.prompt: A unit vector in the direction (3, 4) has what x coordinate?
hints: Find the vector's length first.
Divide the x coordinate by the length.
Write the fraction as a decimal.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The length is 5, so the first unit coordinate is 3/5 = 0.6.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the coordinate before dividing by the length.
That is the y coordinate. The question asks for x.

questions.onCorrect: 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6. Divide each coordinate by the length.

questions.prompt: A unit vector in the direction (0, −7) has what y coordinate?
hints: Find the length first. It is positive.
Divide the y coordinate by the length.
A negative number divided by a positive number is negative.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Its length is 7; the second unit coordinate is −7/7 = −1.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the coordinate before dividing by the length.
The sign is missing. A negative coordinate divided by a positive length stays negative.

questions.onCorrect: −7 ÷ 7 = −1. This vector already points along an axis, so its unit vector is that axis direction.

questions.prompt: Can the game find a direction from (0, 0) by dividing by its length?
hints: Work out its length before trying to divide.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: No. Its length is zero, and you cannot divide by zero.

misconceptions.feedback: Check the length of (0, 0). You cannot divide by that.

questions.onCorrect: The zero vector has length zero and no direction, so it cannot be normalised.

hints: Check the dot product, then check both lengths.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Their dot product is zero, but their lengths are 2 and 3, not 1.

misconceptions.feedback: Orthonormal needs unit length as well. Check how long each vector is.
Their dot product is zero, so they are orthogonal.

questions.onCorrect: The dot product is zero, so they are orthogonal. Their lengths are not 1, so not orthonormal.

hints: Multiply corresponding coordinates.
The second product is negative.
Add the two products. Do they cancel?

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The products 2 and −2 add to zero.

misconceptions.feedback: Check the sign of the second product: one entry is negative.

questions.prompt: A unit vector in the direction (8, −6) has what x coordinate?
hints: Find the length first.
Square each coordinate and add. The length is the root of that sum.
Divide the x coordinate by that length, as a decimal.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the coordinate before dividing by the length.
That is the size of the y coordinate. The question asks for x.
